storage_extensions.usage: MANDATORY. mmap codes.bin as `const uint16_t* prefix_codes` (29.5MB). At startup resolve `japan_code` and `usa_code` by linear-scanning dict.offsets+dict.data once (~19K entries, <1ms): for each dict id i (0-based), if dict.offsets[i+1]-dict.offsets[i] == 5 && memcmp(&dict.data[dict.offsets[i]], "Japan", 5)==0 then japan_code = (uint16_t)(i+1); similarly for "USA" (len 3). If either resolves to 0 (not found), treat that branch as a no-op. The prefix_codes array drives the entire mi scan in this iteration.

join_order.build: prefix_codes column (storage extension, 29.5MB uint16 over all mi rows)
join_order.probe: movie_info rows scanned SEQUENTIALLY in row order (NOT via CSR)
join_order.notes: DIRECTION CHANGE vs iter_2/iter_3: drop the it_rd CSR as the scan driver. Walk r=0..N_mi-1 sequentially; the dominant filter is prefix_codes[r] in {japan_code, usa_code}. Sequential read of 29.5MB across 12 threads is bandwidth-bound (~1-2ms) and far cheaper than the CSR's strided access into 58MB mi_movie_id + 118MB mi_info_off + 626MB mi_info_dat.

join_order.probe: mi row r AFTER prefix passes
join_order.notes: Only ~30K-60K rows pass the prefix filter (very rare globally); read mi_info_type_id[r] only for those — random reads into 58MB are cheap when the set is tiny.

join_order.build: title bitset Y over title.id where production_year > 2000 AND != INT32_MIN
join_order.probe: mv = mi_movie_id[r] for survivors of prefix AND info_type
join_order.notes: Y is ~316KB (L2-resident). Survivors at this point are tiny (~few K) so probing 58MB mi_movie_id incurs only a few K random reads.

join_order.build: mi rows passing prefix AND info_type AND Y AND memmem('200', tail)
join_order.notes: Only after prefix+itid+year all pass do we touch varlen mi_info.off / mi_info.dat. Re-skip-prefix-bytes (Japan: = 6, USA: = 4) and run memmem('200', 3) over the suffix.
For each mv, walk mc range; require any cn_country_code[company_id-1]==cc_us.
For each mv, walk ci range; cheap int filters first (role_id==rt_actress, person_role_id != INT32_MIN), then P_and_an bit test, then varlen note voice-set.
gender=='f' AND name LIKE '%An%' AND aka_name range non-empty. ~520KB → L2.

filters.predicate: gender='f' AND name LIKE '%An%' AND aka_name nonempty
prefix_code in {japan,usa} AND info_type_id=it_rd AND Y[movie_id] AND info LIKE 'Japan:%200%' OR 'USA:%200%'
note IN voice-set AND role_id=rt_actress AND person_role_id present

scan.table: movie_info (sequential over ALL rows, prefix-code driven)
scan.access_pattern: sequential over r=0..N_mi-1 on prefix_codes; rare random reads on other columns for prefix survivors only

data_structures.dim_scalars: int32 ids for rt_actress, it_rd; int16 cc_us; int8 g_f; uint16 japan_code, usa_code resolved from prefix dict at startup
data_structures.Y_year_bitset: vector<uint64_t> sized (N_title+1) bits; bit mv set iff production_year[mv-1] > 2000 AND != INT32_MIN. ~316KB → L2-resident.
data_structures.P_fused_bitset: vector<uint64_t> sized (N_name+1) bits; bit pid set iff name[pid-1].gender=='f' AND memmem(name[pid-1],'An') AND an_off[pid+1] > an_off[pid]. ~520KB → L2-resident.
data_structures.prefix_codes: mmap const uint16_t* (29.5MB); SEQUENTIAL scan driver — replaces the it_rd CSR walk entirely
data_structures.mi_itid: mmap const int32_t* (59MB); read only for prefix survivors
data_structures.aggregation: two scalar MIN accumulators (name_id, title_id), per-thread local then reduce

parallelism.morsel_unit: Y/P bitset builds: parallel for over rows. Mi prefix-driven scan: parallel for over r in [0,N_mi) with static schedule(65536) — large morsels for max sequential prefetch on prefix_codes. Main scan: parallel for over T static schedule(64). Per-thread local accumulators + per-thread local_T vector, merged after.

indexes.purpose: join_lookup ci rows by movie_id in main scan
join_lookup mc rows by movie_id in main scan
consumed only during P_fused_bitset build; not touched during main scan

indexes_intentionally_unused.reason: iter_4 abandons CSR-driven scan; sequential prefix_codes scan is faster because it touches 29.5MB of contiguous uint16 instead of strided access into 58MB mi_movie_id + 118MB mi_info_off + 626MB mi_info_dat. The it_rd filter is applied to prefix-passing rows via mi_info_type_id[r] direct read (a few K random reads, free).

like_strategies.method: Two-stage. Stage 1 (driver): in the main mi scan, read prefix_codes[r] (one uint16) and require code == japan_code OR code == usa_code. NO varlen read at this stage. Stage 2 (survivor verification): only for rows passing prefix AND mi_info_type_id[r]==it_rd AND Y[mv]: read mi_info bytes, skip past the known prefix length (6 for Japan, 4 for USA), and run memmem(suffix, suffix_len, "200", 3). The prefix length is known because the prefix code already tells us which branch we're in.

scan_mi_prefix_driven_filter_order: 5. if (!branch_is_japan && !branch_is_usa) continue; — this is the dominant filter (~99.7% reject), no further memory touched
9. read mi_info bytes [off[r], off[r+1]); skip prefix_len (6 if branch_is_japan else 4); require memmem(suffix, suffix_len, "200", 3)
11. after parallel region: gather, sort, dedupe into T
main_scan_filter_order: 2. mc range walk: require any cn_country_code[company_id-1]==cc_us; break on first hit
3. ci range walk: require role_id==rt_actress (cheap int compare)
5. pid = ci.person_id; require P_and_an bit set (single L2-resident bit test)
6. require ci.note voice-set (varlen, only for rare survivors)
7. update local MIN(name) and (once per movie) MIN(title)
optimization_notes: Iter_4 takes a DIFFERENT direction from iter_3 (which regressed). Root cause: scan_mi at 24ms (38% of total) is dominated by strided access into mi_movie_id (58MB), mi_info_off (118MB), and mi_info_dat (626MB) while walking the it_rd CSR slice (8M rows). All three are L3-exceeding and accessed in strided/random fashion. Strategy: Category B (algorithm change) + Category E (use storage extension). Abandon the CSR-driven scan entirely. Drive the scan with a SEQUENTIAL pass over the 29.5MB prefix_codes column (storage extension): each thread sweeps a contiguous range of mi rows, doing one uint16 compare per row. The prefix filter rejects ~99.7% of rows (only ~30K-60K of 14.8M mi rows have Japan/USA prefix), and rejected rows incur zero further memory touches. For the tiny prefix-surviving set we read mi_info_type_id, mi_movie_id, then Y bitset, then varlen mi_info — all cheap because the set is small. This converts 58MB+118MB+626MB strided/random access into 29.5MB sequential access. Expected scan_mi: 24ms -> 3-5ms. To prevent the codegen regression seen in iter_2 and iter_3 (where prefix_dict was prescribed but not actually mmap'd), the storage_extensions.usage and scan_mi_prefix_driven_filter_order sections give the exact code structure. Year threshold 2000 and the four voice-note strings are preserved verbatim.
